description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Representative John Garamendi (D-CA), a member of the House Armed Services Committee, says "absolutely not" to approving a $1.5 trillion defense budget or money above current appropriations without a clear justification, Representative Mike Lawler (R-NY), chair of the House Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on the Middle East and North Africa, says getting enriched uranium out of Iran is the "largest part" of any Iran deal, and David Kennedy, Dell CFO, says the increase in AI server demand is why the company boosted its annual sales forecast. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US, Iran Agree to 60-Day Truce Pending Trump Approval | Balance of Power: Late Edition 5/28/2026

description: Representative John Garamendi (D-CA), a member of the House Armed Services Committee, says "absolutely not" to approving a $1.5 trillion defense budget or money above current appropriations without a clear justification. He says the Iran war has shown Tehran it has "enormous leverage" over the Strait of Hormuz and any deal should at minimum restore open oil shipping and restart nuclear talks. Rep. Garamendi also argues Congress must reassert its war powers, saying President Trump is "clearly outside of the constitutional boundaries," and reacts to the FCC moving up the expiration of ABC station licenses. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg's Balance of Power. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Rep. Garamendi on Defense Spending, Iran

description: Representative Mike Lawler (R-NY), chair of the House Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on the Middle East and North Africa, says getting enriched uranium out of Iran is the "largest part" of any Iran deal, calling it vital to President Trump and to ensuring Tehran does not get a nuclear weapon. He says a war powers resolution would only bolster Iran during negotiations, and defends Trump's dismissal of midterm politics, saying he cares more about the long-term stability and safety of Americans than "a single election." He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg's Balance of Power. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Rep. Lawler: Uranium Is 'Biggest Part' of Iran Deal

description:
Oil pared gains on a report that the US and Iran have reached a preliminary agreement to extend the ceasefire between the two countries and launch negotiations on the Islamic Republic’s nuclear program.

The memorandum of understanding would extend the truce by 60 days and states that shipping through the vital Strait of Hormuz would be “unrestricted,” without any tolls paid to Iran, but the potential pact still requires President Trump’s approval, Axios reported. Trump wants several days to mull over the deal, according to the report.

An agreement to extend the truce would represent a diplomatic breakthrough and potentially bring the US and Iran closer to reopening normal maritime traffic through the strait, which usually carries around a fifth of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas supply. For more, we speak with Mike McGlone, Senior Commodity Strategist for Bloomberg Intelligence. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Oil Pares Gain on News of Possible US-Iran Pact to Extend Truce
